source.anchor: standard bounded stopping consequence for a square-integrable real Ito integral; Samplinglib completed-process formulation
source.original_text: Let eta be a progressively measurable real integrand that is square-integrable on a positive finite horizon T, let B be Brownian motion relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, and let tau be a nonnegative stopping time satisfying tau(omega) <= T for every omega. Then the completed Ito integral process I_t = integral_0^t eta_s dB_s evaluated at tau is integrable. This is a bounded global-L2 statement; it asserts nothing about unbounded stopping times, local-L2 integrands before localization, vector stochastic integration, quadratic variation, or Ito's formula.

lean.statement:
theorem itoIntegralProcess_at_boundedStopping_integrable
    [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    (eta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (tau : Omega → ℝ≥0)
    (htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration
      (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)))
    (htauT : ∀ omega, tau omega ≤ T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu) :
    Integrable
      (fun omega => itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega) mu
lean.compiler_evidence: Lean 4.33.0 production module and focused Tests/BoundedStoppedItoMean.lean passed.
decoder_context: A filtration indexed by nonnegative reals is a monotone family of measurable subspaces on the sample space.
A ProgressiveL2Integrand is a real progressively measurable integrand with finite product-space L2 norm on the stated finite horizon.
An IsChewiStoppingTime condition says that every event where the nonnegative stopping time is at most a deterministic time is measurable at that time.
IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration supplies the real Brownian-motion contract relative to the displayed filtration and measure.
SatisfiesUsualConditions records completeness and right-continuity of the filtration.
itoIntegralProcess is the constructed completed continuous real Ito integral process; Integrable and the displayed integral are Mathlib Bochner-integral notions.

publication_context.current_lean_module:
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.RandomStoppingGeneralIto

/-!
# Mean of a completed Itô process at a bounded stopping time

For a progressive square-integrable integrand on a finite horizon, the
completed Itô process evaluated at a stopping time bounded by that horizon is
integrable and has mean zero.

The proof applies the martingale mean identity to the completed Itô process of
the stopped integrand.  The completed random-stopping theorem then identifies
its terminal value with evaluation of the original continuous process at the
stopping time.  No optional-sampling theorem beyond the deterministic-time
martingale identity is required.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory
namespace TechnicalLemmas
namespace StochasticProcesses
namespace BoundedStoppedItoMean

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped NNReal

open BrownianMotion ItoIntegralProcess ProgressiveL2 ProgressiveL2Stopping
  RandomStoppingGeneralIto StoppingTime

variable {Omega : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace Omega}
  {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 m} {mu : Measure Omega} {T : ℝ≥0}
  {B : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ}

/-- The completed Itô process is integrable when evaluated at a stopping time
that is pointwise bounded by its construction horizon. -/
theorem itoIntegralProcess_at_boundedStopping_integrable
    [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    (eta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (tau : Omega → ℝ≥0)
    (htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration
      (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)))
    (htauT : ∀ omega, tau omega ≤ T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu) :
    Integrable
      (fun omega => itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega) mu := by
  let _ : IsProbabilityMeasure mu := hB.isProbabilityMeasure
  let stoppedEta := stop eta (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) htau
  have hterminal :
      terminalRepresentative stoppedEta hT hB =ᵐ[mu]
        (fun omega => itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega) := by
    exact (itoIntegralTerminal_stop_ae eta hT tau htau htauT hB hUsual)
  exact (terminalRepresentative_integrable stoppedEta hT hB).congr hterminal

/-- The completed Itô process has mean zero when evaluated at a stopping time
that is pointwise bounded by its construction horizon. -/
theorem integral_itoIntegralProcess_at_boundedStopping_eq_zero
    [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    (eta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (tau : Omega → ℝ≥0)
    (htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration
      (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)))
    (htauT : ∀ omega, tau omega ≤ T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu) :
    ∫ omega, itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega ∂mu = 0 := by
  let _ : IsProbabilityMeasure mu := hB.isProbabilityMeasure
  let stoppedEta := stop eta (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) htau
  have hmartingale :
      Martingale (itoIntegralProcess stoppedEta hT hB hUsual) filtration mu :=
    itoIntegralProcess_martingale stoppedEta hT hB hUsual
  have hterminalMean :
      ∫ omega, terminalRepresentative stoppedEta hT hB omega ∂mu = 0 := by
    have hmean := hmartingale.setIntegral_eq (show (0 : ℝ≥0) ≤ T from bot_le)
      (MeasurableSet.univ : MeasurableSet[filtration 0] Set.univ)
    have hprocessMean :
        ∫ omega, itoIntegralProcess stoppedEta hT hB hUsual T omega ∂mu = 0 := by
      simpa only [Measure.restrict_univ, itoIntegralProcess_at_zero,
        Pi.zero_apply, integral_zero] using hmean.symm
    exact integral_congr_ae
      (terminalRepresentative_ae_eq_actual stoppedEta hT hB hUsual) |>.trans hprocessMean
  calc
    ∫ omega, itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega ∂mu =
        ∫ omega, terminalRepresentative stoppedEta hT hB omega ∂mu := by
          apply integral_congr_ae
          exact (itoIntegralTerminal_stop_ae eta hT tau htau htauT hB hUsual).symm
    _ = 0 := hterminalMean

end BoundedStoppedItoMean
end StochasticProcesses
end TechnicalLemmas
end AutoSamplingTheory

publication_context.statement: For a progressive square-integrable real integrand on a positive finite horizon, evaluating its completed continuous Ito process at a nonnegative stopping time bounded pointwise by the horizon gives an integrable random variable of expectation zero.
assumptions: A progressive L2 integrand on a positive NNReal horizon T.
A Brownian motion relative to the filtration and ambient measure, and the usual filtration conditions.
An NNReal-valued stopping time tau with tau(omega)≤T for every omega.
An ambient finite-measure instance, already entailed by the Brownian probability contract and used by the completed-process API.

obligations.label: Transfer terminal L2 integrability to bounded random-time evaluation
Derive zero expectation from the stopped-integrand martingale and random-stopping identity

lesson.title: A completed Ito process is integrable at a bounded stopping time
lesson.statement: Let eta be progressive and square-integrable on a positive finite horizon T, and let tau be a nonnegative stopping time with tau at most T pointwise. The completed Ito process I(eta) evaluated at tau is integrable.
assumptions: eta is a Samplinglib ProgressiveL2Integrand on a positive NNReal horizon T.
B is Brownian with respect to the filtration and measure; this contract implies that the measure is a probability measure.
The filtration satisfies Samplinglib's usual conditions.
tau is an NNReal-valued Chewi stopping time and tau(omega)≤T for every omega.
Lean requests an ambient finite-measure instance to elaborate the completed process; this is logically redundant because the Brownian contract supplies a probability measure.

steps.title: Stop the integrand
steps.text: Form the closed stopped integrand eta times the indicator of s≤tau. It remains progressive and L2 on the same horizon.

steps.title: Use terminal L2 integrability
steps.text: The terminal representative of the completed Ito integral of the stopped integrand belongs to L2, hence to L1 on the finite measure space.

steps.title: Identify random evaluation
steps.text: The completed bounded random-stopping theorem identifies that terminal representative almost everywhere with the original continuous Ito process evaluated at tau. Integrability transfers across almost-everywhere equality.

lesson.lean_statement: The theorem returns literal Bochner integrability of omega ↦ itoIntegralProcess eta ... (tau omega) omega under the ambient measure, with an explicit finite-measure typeclass already entailed by the Brownian contract.
lesson.lean_proof: The proof transfers the existing L1 property of the stopped terminal representative through the library's completed random-stopping almost-everywhere identity.
